candidates.visible_reason: The wooden tie surface on the left shows heavy graining with long cracks and splits running along the wood. Some edges look rough or frayed, and there is a dark gap near the upper edge where the surface appears separated. Wood fibres look weathered and grey-brown.
candidates.uncertainty: medium: cracking and weathering are clearly visible, but surface checking is common on aged wood and the photo cannot show how deep the cracks go.
alternatives: normal surface checking on weathered wood

candidates.uncertainty: high: the piece is partly covered by stones and shadow, so it is unclear whether it is attached to the tie or is separate debris.
alternatives: loose wood debris resting on the ballast

shadow hiding the true tie outline
